source.title: Crossing the Margin Cliff: Toward Relearn-Robust LLM Unlearning via Margin Calibration
source.authors: Xiangyu Yin; Jiaxu Liu; Zhen Chen; Chih-Hong Cheng

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text contains the full paper and appendices through the compute-budget section.
record.tranche_reason: Tests relearning vulnerability with TOFU and other benchmarks, including small-set fine-tuning attacks, and reports a new counter-method rather than reproducing one of the cited original methods.
record.gate_note: The paper directly tests recovery by fine-tuning on a subset of forget examples and tests Margin Calibration against relearning. It does not test activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompt-only rephrasing, jailbreaks, languages, or in-context information. Its soft-prompt attack optimizes a learned prompt; it is not prompt-only rephrasing. It does not report a never-saw-the-knowledge control for the relearning results.
record.test_reason: The study runs small-set relearning attacks (K forget-set examples via LoRA, FPFT or soft prompts) on 14 unlearning methods and reports held-out forget ROUGE-L. This tests A and B. It also tests its own counter-method, Margin Calibration (MC), against these attacks, which bears on F. There is no activation ablation, quantization or prompt-only attack.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also claim a mechanism: baselines stop above a 'margin cliff' set by retain-regularized stationarity, and a non-saturating margin hinge (MC) crosses it. MC lowers relearn recovery in every populated cell, at a substantial utility cost, with MIA overshoot and UNDIAL exceptions.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces Margin Calibration rather than reproducing a cited original method. It polishes an already-unlearned checkpoint with LoRA, retaining the base loss and adding a reference-anchored non-saturating margin hinge and a KL probe; the deployment variant uses a different anchor and retain-side hinge.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports method- and benchmark-dependent utility costs, weaker MC cliff crossing for UNDIAL, size-dependent MMLU damage, and different membership-inference outcomes on MUSE-News. Its fixed MC configuration is reused across the reported sweeps.

fits_no_version.finding: Baselines' per-token forget margins stop in a band above the retain reference in 41/42 method–size cells (the 'margin cliff'). The cliff gap correlates with relearn recovery (Spearman 0.78–0.91).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shallow unlearning shows up as a residual forget-token margin above a retain-only reference, and that margin predicts relearnability.

record.problems: The authors report substantial TOFU MU loss from MC, only 2/14 MC forget-quality KS p-values above 0.05 at 1B forget10, MIA overshoot past chance, capability collapses in some settings, and a less effective MC result for UNDIAL. The baseline and MC forget/utility columns in Table 1 use different evaluators, although the authors provide a same-evaluator check. No never-saw-knowledge control is reported for the relearning comparison.
record.rows_left_out: At the 60-row cap, did not extract the per-method K20-FPFT values (the aggregate 46/46 result is included in r58), all K-budget and larger-rank/soft-prompt attack cells, the 97-cell per-axis breakdown, or the detailed results for other model sizes, forget tiers, seeds, deployment sweeps, and appendix ablations. These are reported across Tables 2, 6–11, 15, 17–22, and 25–29 and Figures 2, 5, and 6.

untested.parts: Attacks other than relearning on forget subsets; WMDP-style hazardous-knowledge accuracy near chance.
Relearning on unrelated or loosely related data; only subsets of the forget set are used.
Activation-direction ablation and block-vs-delete analysis (a linear probe is mentioned but not reported).
Rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages and in-context information. Soft prompts are optimized inputs, not prompt-only attacks.
Resistance to quantization, activation ablation or prompt-only attacks; FPFT on 3B, MUSE and Phi.

missing.what: Zero-shot MMLU, baseline versus MC, at 1B/3B/8B. MC collapses three methods near chance at 1B; JensUn collapses at 3B/8B.
MUSE-News unpolished pre-attack f-ROUGE (0.047) versus post-attack K20-LoRA (0.053): little relearning recovery.
Baseline relearn recovery at 3B, 8B, forget01/05 and Phi (e.g. 8B baseline K20 0.25–0.61).

record.verdict_notes: The F evidence is the authors' own method. Baseline and MC columns in Table 1 use different evaluators. The reader swapped MIA.agg values into MU rows r16–r18. No never-saw-knowledge relearning control is reported. The reader's version codes V1/V2/V6 were mapped to A/B/F.

versions.untested_parts: No direct test of every condition implied by near-chance targeted accuracy plus broadly preserved general capability; TOFU MU and MMLU are reported, but the MC utility cost is substantial in some settings.
The relearning examples are a subset of the forget set; unrelated or loosely related examples are not tested.
No activation-direction ablation or direct test of whether knowledge is blocked from access rather than deleted.
No prompt-only rephrasing, jailbreak, language-switch, or in-context-information attack.
The paper tests MC against fine-tuning and learned soft prompts, but not against activation ablation, quantization, or prompt-only attacks.
